claims.text: It is the only option that gives you a real Chrome side panel, which is an extension page with access to every Chrome API [1].
The site declares `DRAFT`, `POKEDATA`, `POKEMON_NAMES` and `HEIGHT_DM` as top-level `const` in classic scripts [15][16][17], so `window.DRAFT` is undefined.
Reaching them would need a main-world script plus a `postMessage` relay [3][11] (analysis: bundling is simpler and keeps working if the page changes).
A plain isolated content script can read the run straight from localStorage, because content scripts share storage with the page [8].
It reads the clicked Pokémon from the pick list's `canvas.thumb[data-id]` [14].
It forwards both with `chrome.runtime.sendMessage`, which reaches the side panel [7].
One change to the brief's design: clicking a lineup spot while a pick is pending places the Pokémon immediately [14].

| **MV3 extension + `chrome.sidePanel`** | Developer mode, then Load unpacked, once [9] | Yes, Chrome 114+, can be limited to one site [1][2] | localStorage directly [8]; globals only with `world: "MAIN"` [4] | Delegated DOM listeners | **Recommended** |
| Userscript (Tampermonkey/Violentmonkey) | Install a manager, then turn on its per-extension "Allow User Scripts" toggle (Chrome 138+) [18]; Violentmonkey ships an MV3 build [19] | No.
You inject a floating `div` into the page, and the site's `style-src` blocks injected `<style>` tags and `style=` attributes [25] | Globals via `unsafeWindow` [20] | Yes | Solid fallback |

| Separate local app | High | Its own window | Can't read another origin's storage [23]; the DevTools bridge needs a separate Chrome profile since Chrome 136 [24]; the site can't be iframed [13] | Only through the DevTools Protocol | Not worth it |
**Service worker** (`service-worker.js`): calls `chrome.sidePanel.setPanelBehavior({ openPanelOnActionClick: true })` so the toolbar icon opens the panel [2].
That is the official site-specific sample [2].
reads `JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('pokemon-all22-draft-v1'))` [8]
posts `{state, focusId}` with `chrome.runtime.sendMessage` [7]
loads its bundled `pokemon.js`, `pokedata.js` and `draft.js` with classic `<script>` tags in that order, the same order as the site [13]
listens on `chrome.runtime.onMessage` [6]
when it opens, asks the content script for the current state with `chrome.tabs.sendMessage(tabId, …)`, because `runtime.sendMessage` can't reach content scripts [7]
A delegated listener runs `e.target.closest('.cand')`, then `.querySelector('canvas.thumb').dataset.id`, and gets the dex id [14].
**Detecting changes.** The `storage` event never fires in the tab that made the change [10].
The app sets it to `setup`, `turn`, `placing` or `done` on every phase change [14].
Heavier option: a `world: "MAIN"` script at `document_start` that wraps `Storage.prototype.setItem` and relays each write with `window.postMessage` [3][11].
They share the DOM but can't see the page's JS variables [3].

`"world": "MAIN"` in the manifest (Chrome 111+ [12]) or `chrome.scripting.executeScript({world: 'MAIN'})` (Chrome 95+ [5]) runs code in the page's own environment, where the bare name `DRAFT` would resolve.
The Chrome docs warn that the page can interfere with such scripts [4].
MAIN-world scripts can't use `chrome.runtime` and have to relay through the shared DOM or `postMessage` [11][3].
The site's private state (`draft`, `lineup`, `SLOTS`) sits inside app.js's IIFE (immediately-invoked function), so no world can reach it [14].
A minimal manifest, assembled from the docs (Medium confidence) [1][2][4]:
**`side_panel.default_path`:** the site-specific sample leaves it out and sets `path` per tab, so the panel exists only on the target site [2].
**Optional permissions:** add `"scripting"` only if you use `executeScript` [5], and `"storage"` only if you use `chrome.storage.session` as a shared store.
Content scripts need `setAccessLevel` to use that store [8].
**Keyboard shortcut:** the sample binds `_execute_action` to Command+B on macOS to toggle the panel [2].
**Opening the panel:** `sidePanel.open()` needs Chrome 116+ and must run in response to a user action [1].
**Loading it:** go to chrome://extensions, turn on Developer mode, then Load unpacked [9].
Extension HTML pages need no extension reload [9].

claims.text: **151 Challenge:** has no pick list and saves under `pokemon-all22-151-v1` [14].
The live files matched the earlier local copies as of 2026-10-14 [13].
**Selectors change.** `.cand`, `canvas.thumb[data-id]` and `.hotspot[data-slot]` all come from app.js and can be renamed without warning [14].
**Writes go through one function.** The run key is written only by `saveDraft()` → `saveRun()` [14].
Signed-in runs also end in `saveDraft()`, but whether every server field gets copied was not checked (Medium) [14].
**MAIN-world scripts are exposed.** The page can access and tamper with them [4].
Reload the game tab too [9].
**Bookmarklets under a strict CSP.** The site sends `script-src 'self'` with no `'unsafe-inline'` [13].
The CSP3 spec says page policy "SHOULD NOT interfere with … bookmarklets" [22].
MDN lists `javascript:` URLs as inline script that this policy blocks [21].
**Source for "Chrome 111+" on manifest `world`.** MDN's compatibility data says 111 [12].
Google's own pages give no version [4].
That comes from standard JS semantics [15].
